findings.claim: remove-vault-login-mfa.md Step 2 tells the reader to run `just mfa_status` right after `cd deployments/infrastructure`, but that directory's justfile has no mfa_status recipe, so just fails with "justfile does not contain recipe `mfa_status`". The sibling MFA pages say to run it from the repository root.
send-python-traces-to-tempo.md says the task needs "Docker's `network_mode = "host"`, as embark uses". embark, like every job in the repo, uses the podman driver. No job uses the docker driver.

test-acme-job-changes-on-staging.md Step 2 says `nomad job status acme` finds "the child's allocation ID". For a periodic parent it lists child jobs (acme/periodic-<id>), not allocations, so the reader needs `nomad job status acme/periodic-<id>` as check-the-edge-certificate.md already shows.

verdict.text: The audit holds up.

Every procedural fix I checked against the code is right, and several fix real errors in the old pages: the driftwatch baseline is on a dynamic host volume, so the old SSH path was wrong; the Consul client agents run `down_policy = "deny"`, so the old extend-cache claim was false; and deleting the MFA blocks with `vault delete` while Terraform still declares them would have caused a lockout.
Three small doc errors remain, and none needs another review round, so the verdict is fix.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: pass on gate pre_commit, gate cli_tests and rows r1, r2, r3, r4 and r6, ending "stamp green: 88e7ac632875fbd7f24e838ea5aae7ada7d05a8b2d3cd52c22f6424dbe577b47".
Rows r1-r4 and r6: read each command.

Each one checks its `fails_when` directly (front matter keys, review-due notices, check warnings that name docs/how-to, shorthand tokens against `git ls-files`, and that the note-sync files do not exist).
